words: وَبَدَا لَهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يَكُونُوا۟ يَحْتَسِبُونَ
rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: At resurrection they will see what they had not expected in worldly life would befall them in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: ظهر لهم حين بعثوا ما لم يحتسبوا في الدنيا أنه نازل بهم في الآخرة

words: وَبَدَا لَهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يَكُونُوا۟ يَحْتَسِبُونَ
rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says they thought their deeds were good deeds, but these appeared as evil deeds; their idol worship as devotion to God brought an unforeseen punishment.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: ظنوا أنها حسنات فبدت لهم سيئات، والمعنى: أنهم كانوا يتقربون إلى الله بعبادة الأصنام

words: وَبَدَا لَهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يَكُونُوا۟ يَحْتَسِبُونَ
rows.speaker: محمد بن المنكدر
rows.claim: At death, Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir became distressed and said he feared that what he had not expected would appear to him; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وروي أن محمد بن المنكدر جزع عند الموت، فقيل له في ذلك فقال: أخشى أن يبدو لي ما لم أحتسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil deeds that become manifest are their bad acts of associating partners with God and oppressing God's allies.
rows.anchor: أي: مساوئ أعمالهم من الشرك والظلم بأولياء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ḍurr means hardship or distress.
rows.anchor: فإذا مس الإنسان ضر}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawwalnāhu means that God gave him the blessing.
rows.anchor: ثم إذا خولناه} أعطيناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person claims he received the blessing because God knew he deserved it.
rows.anchor: أي: على علم من الله أني له أهل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil takes the claim to mean that it came through a good quality God knew the person possessed.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: على خير علمه الله عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun is used because the intended noun is al-inʿām, the act of bestowing the blessing.
rows.anchor: وذكر الكناية لأن المراد من النعمة الإنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing is a divine trial, gradual enticement, and affliction.
rows.anchor: استدراج من الله تعالى وامتحان وبلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the utterance itself, rather than the blessing, as the trial.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل كلمته التي قالها فتنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people do not recognize that the blessing is a test and gradual enticement.
rows.anchor: أنه استدراج وامتحان

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil identifies the earlier speaker as Qarun, who said he had been given wealth through knowledge he possessed.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني قارون فإنه قال

words: فَمَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their acquired disbelief did not protect them from punishment at all.
rows.anchor: فما أغنى عنهم الكفر من العذاب شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is illuminated by the light of its Creator when He manifests to judge His creatures.
rows.anchor: أضاءت، {بنور ربها} بنور خالقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that light people are not distressed, just as they are not distressed by sunlight on a clear day.
rows.anchor: فما يتضارون في نوره كما لا يتضارون في الشمس في اليوم الصحو

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets the Lord's light as His justice; the earth means the plains of the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن والسدي: بعدل ربها، وأراد بالأرض عرصات القيامة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the Lord's light as His justice; the earth means the plains of the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن والسدي: بعدل ربها، وأراد بالأرض عرصات القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book placed is the record of deeds.
rows.anchor: {ووضع الكتاب} أي: كتاب الأعمال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the witnesses as the community of Muḥammad, who testify that the messengers delivered their messages.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني الذين يشهدون للرسل بتبليغ الرسالة، وهم أمة محمد

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ identifies the witnesses as the recording angels and cites Q 50:21 as support.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: يعني الحفظة، يدل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The judgment between them is just.
rows.anchor: {وقضي بينهم بالحق} أي: بالعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are not wronged: no bad deed is added and no good deed is subtracted.
rows.anchor: {وهم لا يظلمون} أي: لا يزاد في سيئاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every soul receives the recompense for what it did.
rows.anchor: {ووفيت كل نفس ما عملت} أي: ثواب ما عملت

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ explains that God already knows their deeds and needs neither a recorder nor a witness.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: يريد أني عالم بأفعالهم لا أحتاج إلى كاتب ولا إلى شاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are driven forcefully toward Hell.
rows.anchor: {وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم} سوقا عنيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They go in successive groups, each community apart from the others.
rows.anchor: {زمرا} أفواجا بعضها على إثر بعض، كل أمة على حدة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأخفش
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Akhfash gloss zumaran as separate companies; its singular is zumra.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة والأخفش: "زمرا" أي: جماعات في تفرقة، واحدتها زمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell has seven gates, which had been closed before the disbelievers arrived.
rows.anchor: {حتى إذا جاءوها فتحت أبوابها} السبعة وكانت مغلقة قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kūfan readers recite the verb without doubling its middle consonant; the other readers double it to convey repeated opening.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة "فتحت، وفتحت" بالتخفيف، وقرأ الآخرون بالتشديد على التكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers address them in rebuke and reproach.
rows.anchor: {وقال لهم خزنتها} توبيخا وتقريعا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers were from among the disbelievers' own people.
rows.anchor: {ألم يأتكم رسل منكم} من أنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaqqat means that the word of punishment became binding.
rows.anchor: قالوا بلى ولكن حقت} وجبت، {كلمة العذاب على الكافرين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word of punishment is God's declaration that He will fill Hell with jinn and people.
rows.anchor: وهو قوله عز وجل: "لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment mentioned follows because they disbelieved when their messengers came with clear proofs; God seized them, for He is strong and severe in punishment.
rows.anchor: أي: ذلك العذاب الذي نزل بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent Moses with signs and clear authority to Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun, who called him a lying magician.
rows.anchor: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون فقالوا ساحر كذاب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says this is a renewed killing: Pharaoh had stopped killing boys, then resumed after Moses was sent.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هذا غير القتل الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women were spared so that the believers would be deterred from following and supporting Moses.
rows.anchor: ليصدوهم بذلك عن متابعة موسى ومظاهرته

words: وَمَا كَيْدُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plot is Pharaoh and his people's scheme and contrivance, which comes to nothing and is overtaken by God's purpose.
rows.anchor: وما مكر فرعون وقومه واحتيالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh said this to his court; members of his inner circle were preventing him from killing Moses for fear of ruin.
rows.anchor: لأنه كان في خاصة قوم فرعون من يمنعه من قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh taunts Moses to call the Lord he claims sent him, challenging that Lord to protect him from them.
rows.anchor: أي: وليدع موسى ربه الذي يزعم أنه أرسله إلينا فيمنعه منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yubaddila means to change.
rows.anchor: {إني أخاف أن يبدل} يغير، {دينكم} الذي أنتم عليه

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: يعقوب وأهل الكوفة
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb and the Kūfans read aw an yuzhira, while the others read wa-an yuzhira.
rows.anchor: قرأ يعقوب وأهل الكوفة "أو أن يظهر " وقرأ الآخرون "وأن يظهر "

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة والبصرة وحفص
rows.claim: The Medinans, Basrans, and Ḥafṣ read yuzhira with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on hāʾ, making it transitive; fasād is accusative and coordinates with changing their religion.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة والبصرة وحفص "يظهر" بضم الياء وكسر الهاء

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: The other readers use the intransitive yuzhar, with fasād nominative; the intended corruption is replacing the religion and worshipping another than God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بفتح الياء والهاء على اللزوم، "الفساد" رفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses sought refuge in God after Pharaoh threatened to kill him.
rows.anchor: لما توعده فرعون بالقتل، {إني عذت بربي وربكم

rows.speaker: مقاتل والسدي
rows.claim: Muqātil and al-Suddī say the believer was an Egyptian, Pharaoh's cousin, and the man described in Q 28:20.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل والسدي: كان قبطيا ابن عم فرعون

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say the believing man was an Israelite, with min āli Firʿawn understood as describing whom he concealed his faith from.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: كان إسرائيليا، ومجاز الآية: وقال رجل مؤمن يكتم إيمانه من آل فرعون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر العلماء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most scholars give the man's name as Ḥuzayl.
rows.anchor: وكان اسمه حزئيل عند ابن عباس، وأكثر العلماء

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq gives the man's name as Jibrān.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: كان اسمه [جبران]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported name for the believer is Ḥabīb.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان اسم الرجل الذي آمن من آل فرعون حبيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase an yaqūla means because he says, 'My Lord is God.'
rows.anchor: {أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله} لأن يقول ربي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proofs are what indicate Moses' truthfulness.
rows.anchor: أي: بما يدل على صدقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Moses is lying, the liability for his lie is his own and it will not harm you.
rows.anchor: {وإن يك كاذبا فعليه كذبه}

words: وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقًۭا يُصِبْكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى يَعِدُكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Moses is truthful and they reject him, some of what he threatens will reach them.
rows.anchor: فكذبتموه، {يصبكم بعض الذي يعدكم}

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says baʿḍ, 'some,' means the whole: if they kill Moses while he is truthful, all the threatened punishment will strike them.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: المراد بالبعض الكل، أي: إن قتلتموه وهو صادق أصابكم ما يتوعدكم به من العذاب

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth treats baʿḍ as an additional particle, so the sense is that what Moses promises will strike them.
rows.anchor: قال الليث: "بعض" صلة، يريد

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The rhetoricians retain the ordinary sense 'some': even a portion of the threatened punishment would mean their destruction, so mention of a part establishes the whole.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: هذا على الظاهر في الحجاج كأنه قال: أقل ما في صدقه أن يصيبكم بعض الذي يعدكم

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌۭ كَذَّابٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mus'rif here means an associator of partners with God, and kadhdhāb means a liar against God.
rows.anchor: إلى دينه، {من هو مسرف}

words: أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmr told ʿUrwa that the worst assault on the Prophet was when ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ choked him at the Kaʿba; Abū Bakr intervened and quoted the believer's words. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: قلت لعبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: أخبرني بأشد ما صنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene is the people of Hell disputing there, which Muḥammad is told to recall to his people.
rows.anchor: أي: اذكر يا محمد لقومك إذ يختصمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weak say they followed the arrogant in worldly life and ask if they can now bear a share of the fire for them.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا، {فهل أنتم مغنون عنا نصيبا من النار}

rows.speaker: أهل البصرة
rows.claim: Basran scholars say tabaʿ can be both singular and plural, with tābiʿ as its singular form.
rows.anchor: والتبع يكون واحدا وجمعا في قول أهل البصرة، وواحده تابع

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: Kūfan scholars treat tabaʿ as a collective plural with no singular; its plural is atbāʿ.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل الكوفة: هو جمع لا واحد له، وجمعه أتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrogant answer that everyone is in Hell and God has already judged between the servants.
rows.anchor: قال الذين استكبروا إنا كل فيها إن الله قد حكم بين العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the Fire make their plea when the punishment has intensified against them.
rows.anchor: في النار} حين اشتد عليهم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask the keepers of Hell to appeal to God to reduce their punishment for one day.
rows.anchor: لخزنة جهنم ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers ask whether messengers had come to them with clear proofs; the condemned admit that they had.
rows.anchor: {قالوا} يعني خزنة جهنم لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers tell them to pray for themselves, refusing to pray on their behalf because they know the punishment will not be reduced.
rows.anchor: أنتم إذا ربكم، إنا لا ندعو لكم

words: وَمَا دُعَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' prayer is futile, misguided, and of no benefit to them.
rows.anchor: أي: يبطل ويضل ولا ينفعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two days were Sunday and Monday.
rows.anchor: في يومين} يوم الأحد والاثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rawāsi are firmly fixed mountains above the earth.
rows.anchor: أي في الأرض، {رواسي} جبالا ثوابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God blessed the earth with seas, rivers, trees, and fruits.
rows.anchor: أي: في الأرض، بما خلق فيها من البحار

rows.speaker: الحسن ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Muqātil say God apportioned on earth the provisions of people and animals.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن ومقاتل: قسم في الأرض أرزاق العباد والبهائم

rows.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
rows.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say each region received provisions not found elsewhere, so people sustain one another by trade between regions.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة والضحاك: قدر في كل بلدة ما لم يجعله في الأخرى ليعيش بعضهم من بعض بالتجارة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī gives regional examples: bread, dates, corn, and fish are each provisions of particular districts.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: قدر الخبز لأهل قطر، والتمر لأهل قطر، والذرة لأهل قطر، والسمك لأهل قطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth's contents and provisions were created over Tuesday and Wednesday, completing four days together with Sunday and Monday; the later count includes the earlier days, as in the example of marrying one woman yesterday and two today where one is yesterday's.
rows.anchor: يريد خلق ما في الأرض، وقدر الأقوات في يومين يوم الثلاثاء والأربعاء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ويعقوب والآخرون
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads sawāʾ nominative as a predicate, Yaʿqūb genitive as an adjective to 'four days,' and the others accusative as a verbal noun meaning evenly; the phrase answers how long earth and its provisions took to create.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر "سواء" رفع على الابتداء

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي
rows.claim: Qatāda and al-Suddī say this gives an even, complete answer to anyone asking how long earth and its provisions were created: no addition or reduction.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة والسدي: من سأل عنه فهكذا الأمر سواء لا زيادة ولا نقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istawā ilā al-samāʾ means that God turned to undertake the creation of the sky.
rows.anchor: {ثم استوى إلى السماء} أي: عمد إلى خلق السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The smoke was water vapor.
rows.anchor: {وهي دخان} وكان ذلك الدخان بخار الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to do what God orders, as in the expression 'do what is best.'
rows.anchor: ائتيا ما آمركما أي: افعلاه، كما يقال: ائت ما هو الأحسن، أي: افعله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through Ṭāwūs, glosses iʾtiyā as 'give forth.'
rows.anchor: وقال طاووس عن ابن عباس: ائتيا: أعطيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports God telling the sky to produce the sun, moon, and stars, and the earth to open its rivers and bring forth fruit and vegetation; He said to obey willingly or be compelled, and both obeyed willingly.
rows.anchor: قال الله عز وجل: أما أنت يا سماء فأطلعي شمسك وقمرك ونجومك، وأنت يا أرض فشقي أنهارك وأخرجي ثمارك ونباتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual feminine subjects take the masculine plural ṭāʾiʿīn because the meaning includes the heavens, earth, and those within them; it means they came with what they contain, obediently, and rational speech permits the human plural.
rows.anchor: لأنه ذهب به إلى السموات والأرض ومن فيهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Satan provokes you, seek refuge in God, who hears your plea and words and knows your actions and circumstances.
rows.anchor: استعاذتك وأقوالك، {العليم} بأفعالك وأحوالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night, day, sun, and moon are signs of God's power; worship God alone rather than prostrating to the sun or moon.
rows.anchor: ومن آياته الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر لا تسجدوا للشمس ولا للقمر واسجدوا لله الذي خلقهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine plural pronoun khalaqahunna follows the broken-plural construction and does not use masculine predominance over feminine nouns.
rows.anchor: بالتأنيث لأنه أجراها على طريق جمع التكسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those near their Lord are the angels, who glorify Him night and day without tiring.
rows.anchor: {فإن استكبروا} عن السجود، {فالذين عند ربك} يعني الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is khāshiʿa when it is dry, dusty, and without vegetation.
rows.anchor: يابسة غبراء لا نبات فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water makes the earth stir and swell; the One who revives it is able to raise the dead and is powerful over everything.
rows.anchor: فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت إن الذي أحياها لمحيي الموتى إنه على كل شيء قدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers the believers who do righteous works when they call on Him.
rows.anchor: أي: ويجيب الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās the alternate sense 'He rewards the believers.'
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: ويثيب الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God adds from His favor beyond the recompense due for their works.
rows.anchor: سوى ثواب أعمالهم تفضلا منه

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that God intercedes for them regarding their brothers and extends favor to the brothers of their brothers.
rows.anchor: قال أبو صالح عنه: يشفعهم في إخوانهم، ويزيدهم من فضله. قال: في إخوان إخوانهم

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt says the verse was revealed about them: they saw the wealth of Banū Qurayẓa, Banū al-Naḍīr, and Banū Qaynuqāʿ and wished for it.
rows.anchor: قال خباب بن الأرت: فينا نزلت هذه الآية، وذلك أنا نظرنا إلى أموال بني قريظة وبني النضير وبني قينقاع فتمنيناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghaw means they would become tyrannical and insolent on earth.
rows.anchor: لطغوا وعتوا، {في الأرض}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes their transgression as seeking one status after another, one mount after another, and one kind of clothing after another.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بغيهم طلبهم منزلة بعد منزلة ومركبا بعد مركب وملبسا بعد ملبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God apportions people's provision as He wills, in consideration of His servants; He knows and sees them.
rows.anchor: كما يشاء نظرا منه لعباده

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن النبي عن جبريل عن الله
rows.claim: In a divine report, God says whoever humiliates His ally wages war on Him; He loves obligatory acts and then voluntary acts, answers the loved servant's prayers, and gives some servants wealth or poverty because that condition preserves their faith. The segment's report ends mid-sentence; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن جبريل عن الله عز وجل قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghayth is rain, which God sends after people have despaired of it; this should increase their gratitude.
rows.anchor: المطر، {من بعد ما قنطوا} يعني: من بعد ما يئس الناس منه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says God withheld rain from the people of Mecca for seven years until they despaired, then sent it and reminded them of His favor.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: حبس الله المطر عن أهل مكة سبع سنين حتى قنطوا، ثم أنزل الله المطر فذكرهم الله نعمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spreading of God's mercy means His spreading the rain, as also stated in Q 7:57.
rows.anchor: {وينشر رحمته} يبسط مطره، كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the patron of those who obey Him and is praised among His creatures.
rows.anchor: لأهل طاعته، {الحميد} عند خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering of all the creatures dispersed through the heavens and earth is the gathering on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: يعني: يوم القيامة

words: فَلَوْلَآ أُلْقِىَ عَلَيْهِ أَسْوِرَةٌۭ مِّن ذَهَبٍ
rows.speaker: حفص ويعقوب والآخرون
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ and Yaʿqūb read aswira, a plural of siwār; the others read asāwira, a plural of usūra which is itself a plural.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص ويعقوب "أسورة" جمع سوار، وقرأ الآخرون "أساورة" على جمع الأسورة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says leaders were invested with a gold bracelet and necklace to signal their rule; Pharaoh asks why Moses' Lord did not bestow gold bracelets on him if he was a lord they had to obey.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: كانوا إذا سودوا رجلا سوروه بسوار وطوقوه بطوق من ذهب يكون ذلك دلالة لسيادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels would come in succession, accompanying one another to testify to Moses' truth and assist him.
rows.anchor: متتابعين يقارن بعضهم بعضا يشهدون له بصدقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh made his Egyptian people seem foolish, finding them ignorant.
rows.anchor: أي استخف فرعون قومه القبط، أي وجدهم جهالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is that Pharaoh led them into frivolity and ignorance, removing them from sound judgment.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حملهم على الخفة والجهل. يقال: استخفه عن رأيه، إذا حمله على الجهل وأزاله عن الصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They obeyed Pharaoh by denying Moses, and were a disobedient people.
rows.anchor: على تكذيب موسى، {إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muhl is the black residue at the bottom of oil.
rows.anchor: هو دردي الزيت الأسود

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وحفص والآخرون
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read yaghli with yāʾ, making the verb refer to al-muhl; the others use tāʾ to agree with the feminine tree.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وحفص "يغلي" بالياء، جعلوا الفعل للمهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bellies are those of the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: أي بطون الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boiling is like hot water when it boils intensely.
rows.anchor: كالماء الحار إذا اشتد غليانه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن رسول الله
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet saying that if one drop of Zaqqum fell on earth, it would ruin the livelihood of the world's inhabitants; how terrible for those whose only food is Zaqqum. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is addressed to the infernal guards, and the one they seize is the sinner.
rows.anchor: أي يقال للزبانية: خذوه، يعني الأثيم

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة وأبو جعفر وأبو عمرو والباقون
rows.claim: The Kūfans, Abū Jaʿfar, and Abū ʿAmr read ʿatlihi with kasra on tāʾ; the others use ḍamma, and both are dialects.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة، وأبو جعفر، وأبو عمرو: بكسر التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAtl means to push and drive with force, pulling and dragging him roughly.
rows.anchor: أي ادفعوه وسوقوه، يقال: عتله يعتله عتلا إذا ساقه بالعنف والدفع والجذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ al-jaḥīm means the middle of Hellfire.
rows.anchor: إلى سواء الجحيم} وسطه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says the keeper strikes the man's head until it opens to his brain, then pours in water heated to its limit. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل، إن خازن النار يضربه على رأسه فينقب رأسه عن دماغه، ثم يصب فيه ماء حميما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned is told to taste the punishment.
rows.anchor: ثم يقال له: {ذق} هذا العذاب

rows.speaker: الكسائي والآخرون
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī opens the hamza in annaka, meaning 'because you used to say I am mighty'; the others use kasra and begin a new clause.
rows.anchor: قرأ الكسائي "أنك" بفتح الألف، أي لأنك كنت تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title 'mighty and noble' is attributed to him only by his people and according to his own claim; the keepers say it in contempt and rebuke.
rows.anchor: عند قومك بزعمك، وذلك أن أبا جهل كان يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who listen to Muḥammad are hypocrites who do not understand or heed him, out of disdain and deliberate inattention.
rows.anchor: وهم المنافقون، يستمعون قولك فلا يعونه ولا يفهمونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means 'when they leave your presence.'
rows.anchor: يعني فإذا خرجوا من عندك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of knowledge they question are Companions.
rows.anchor: قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم} من الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ānifan means 'just now'; it derives from beginning or resuming something, and anaf is a thing's beginning.
rows.anchor: يعني الآن، هو من الائتناف

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says the Prophet criticized the hypocrites in his sermon, and on leaving the mosque they mockingly asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd what he had said.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يخطب ويعيب المنافقين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says he too was among those asked.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وقد سئلت فيمن سئل

words: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ طَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sealed their hearts so that they did not believe.
rows.anchor: {أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم} فلم يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They followed their desires in disbelief and hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: في الكفر والنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who are guided are the believers.
rows.anchor: {والذين اهتدوا} يعني المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increased them in guidance through what the Messenger said.
rows.anchor: ما قال الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enabled them to act on what He commanded, which is taqwā.
rows.anchor: وفقهم للعمل بما أمرهم به، وهو التقوى

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the phrase means that God gave them the reward of their taqwā.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: وآتاهم ثواب تقواهم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet listing what people await in worldly life: wealth that corrupts, poverty that makes one forget, damaging illness, enfeebling old age, sudden death, the Dajjāl, or the Hour; the Hour is more calamitous and bitter. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse came down about Thābit ibn Qays insulting a man who did not make room for him, calling him the son of a woman; the Prophet asked who had mentioned the woman, and Thābit admitted it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في ثابت بن قيس، وقوله للرجل الذي لم يفسح له: ابن فلانة، يعيره بأمه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet had Thābit look at the people; when Thābit saw white, red, and black faces, the Prophet said he was superior to them only through religion and piety.
rows.anchor: فقال: انظر في وجوه القوم فنظر فقال: ما رأيت يا ثابت؟ قال: رأيت أبيض وأحمر وأسود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Thābit, and the verse about making room in gatherings was revealed concerning the man who did not make room, Q 58:11.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في ثابت بن قيس، وقوله للرجل الذي لم يفسح له

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says that at the conquest of Mecca the Prophet sent Bilāl to call the adhān from the Kaʿba; ʿAttāb ibn Asīd lamented that his father had died before seeing the day, al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām called Bilāl a black crow, and Suhayl ibn ʿAmr said God would make him change; Abū Sufyān kept silent for fear God in heaven would reveal his words.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: لما كان يوم فتح مكة أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلالا حتى علا ظهر الكعبة وأذن

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Gabriel informed the Prophet of their remarks; he summoned and questioned them, they admitted, and the verse rebuked boasting of lineage and wealth and disparaging the poor.
rows.anchor: فأتى جبريل فأخبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بما قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Male and female means Adam and Eve: people share equal lineage.
rows.anchor: يعني آدم وحواء أي إنكم متساوون في النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿūb is the plural of shaʿb with an open shīn, the highest lineage group and root of tribes, such as Rabīʿa, Muḍar, Aws, and Khazraj; it is named for branching and gathering like the branches of a tree.
rows.anchor: جمع شعب بفتح الشين، وهي رؤوس القبائل مثل ربيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root shaʿb is an antonym: it can mean to gather or to divide.
rows.anchor: والشعب من الأضداد يقال: شعب، أي: جمع، وشعب أي: فرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tribes rank below peoples, as Bakr within Rabīʿa and Tamīm within Muḍar.
rows.anchor: {وقبائل} وهي دون الشعوب، واحدتها قبيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Below tribes come ʿamāʾir, then abṭun, then afkhādh, then faṣāʾil and ʿashāʾir; examples include Shaybān and Dārim, Banū Ghālib and Luʾayy, and Banū Hāshim and Umayya; no lineage group after the ʿashīra is named.
rows.anchor: ودون القبائل العمائر، واحدتها عمارة، بفتح العين، وهم كشيبان من بكر، ودارم من تميم، ودون العمائر البطون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says peoples are non-Arabs, tribes are Arabs, and asbāṭ are the tribes of the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الشعوب من العجم، والقبائل من العرب، والأسباط من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: أبو روق
rows.claim: Abū Rawq says peoples are those who claim no ancestor and affiliate instead with towns and villages, while tribes are Arabs who trace descent through their fathers.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو روق: "الشعوب" الذين لا يعتزون إلى أحد
